thing.text:
RESORT INFINITY

Everything is out the back
door: the cottages, the front
desk, the guests.

Go outside.

thing.label: the mist
thing.note: The row goes on into the mist: cottages 12, 13 and 14 stand in it, and all the rest behind them. A guest sent past 14 walks in and is lost to view. Nothing in the resort knows how many cottages there are.
The resort’s own machinery for everybody already housed, one behaviour per guest, switched on: they are listening for the bell. Nothing in them knows how many guests there are.
This guest’s own robots: ask the desk where to live (with its group number), walk to the cottage it is given, and ask the moving office again when the bell rings.

active.name: Ask for a place

team.name: Move on the bell I kept
team.note: The bell rang before I had a place, and the pad was kept in hole 7. Now that I have one: the same as Move when told to, on the kept pad.

team.name: Move when told to
team.note: A pad has landed on my nest: the bell, rung for every guest. Sends [where I live, my own bird] to the moving office and takes my place out of the box, so that the answer puts a new one in.

team.name: Keep the bell for later
team.note: The bell rang before I had a place (Move when told to did not fit): takes the pad off my nest into hole 7, which uncovers the address under it.

team.name: Stand at my address
team.note: A number has landed on my nest: that is my address. Works out where that cottage stands along the row, remembers it as my place, and walks there.

active.note: Leads. My number is still in the box, so I have nowhere to live: sends [my number, my group, my own bird] to the desk and takes my number out as it goes, so I never ask twice.

holes.note: Rides in the little house behind your robot: once your robot has taken the number off the letter and answered it, sweeps the letter away, and the house folds itself up.

active.name: Run your robot on the letter

team.name: Take the robot in
team.note: A robot has landed on its nest: yours. Takes it into hole 2.

active.note: A letter [number | group | bird] lies on the post and your robot is in hole 2: takes a fresh little house, puts the letter in it, then a copy of your robot with a copy of Tidy behind it, and sets the house down on the grass to work.

holes.name: Tidy
holes.note: Rides in the little house behind your robot: once your robot has answered the letter, sweeps the empty letter away, and the house folds itself up.

active.name: Run your robot on the letter

team.name: Take the robot in
team.note: A robot has landed on its nest: yours. Takes it into hole 2, and rings the bell: the pad "a move, please" to every guest, who then writes where it lives.

active.note: A letter lies on the post and your robot is in hole 2: takes a fresh little house, puts the letter in it, then a copy of your robot with a copy of Tidy behind it, and sets the house down on the grass to work.

thing.text:
RESORT INFINITY 4

Problem 3 is solved: the guests
who were here moved from i to
2i (the even cottages, and on
into the mist), and the gold
group took the odd ones,
2i - 1. The eleven you can see
are full again.

A newcomer writes [my number
| my group | bird] to the
front desk; a housed guest
writes [where I live | bird]
to the moving office.

Set the Speed to 4x or 8x.

PROBLEM 4
Three infinite groups

Three groups arrive at once --
green is group 1, plum group
2, teal group 3 -- each
without end; three of each are
at the gate.

A mover for the office: given
[where I live | bird], where
does a housed guest go so
that THREE cottages in every
four come free?
A clerk for the desk: given
[number | group | bird], where
does guest i of group j go?
Then SPACE on "three groups".

Hint: 4i, and 4i - j. Or
do problem 3 three times.

HOW TO TRAIN ONE

Take a little robot from its
stack and set it on the grass.
Drop a practice letter ON it:
its thought bubble opens and
you are teaching it.

A number from the stack, typed
and dropped on the letter’s
number, adds; Ctrl with the
number held makes it multiply
or subtract (the badge). Then
the number to the bird.

Ruby erases the numbers in
its thought: any will do.
Leave the bubble, click the
robot to pick it up, and give
it to the bird.

THE ROW GOES ON

Eleven cottages stand in
the clear, counted from the
left, and a guest given a
number walks to that cottage.

The row does not stop at 11:
it goes on into the mist.
Cottages 12, 13 and 14 are
in there, and all the rest
behind them, as far as you
like. A guest sent to 15
walks in and is lost to view.

Nothing in these robots knows
how many guests there are.
That is the whole of it.

thing.name: Four times
thing.note: Problem 4, answered: everybody housed moves from i to 4i, which empties three cottages in every four. Given [where I live | bird], drops a x4 on the number, takes it and gives it to the bird.

thing.name: Four apart
thing.note: Problem 4, answered: newcomer i of group j takes cottage 4i - j. Given [number | group | bird], drops a x4 on the number, then a copy of the group with a minus sign, takes the number and gives it to the bird.
